title: Direct comparison with the closest antecedent: global versus locally coupled Hopfield memory and repair at equal state size
question: At equal state size (N = 64 binary cells on an 8x8 grid), how do a global Hopfield network and locally coupled Hopfield networks compare at storing K patterns and repairing them after erasure of a fraction f of cells and additive noise sigma, and how close do they come to an explicit nearest-pattern decoder?
role: Antecedent comparison for the candidate central hypothesis on memory and repair (guide section 18I); exploratory, spends no alpha

patterns.smooth: Gaussian-smoothed (sigma 1.5 cells, reflect boundary) i.i.d. normal field on the 8x8 grid, thresholded at its median

models.global_hopfield: W = (1/N) sum_k xi_k xi_k^T, zero diagonal
models.local_r1: Same Hebbian weights restricted to the 3x3 Moore neighbourhood (open boundary), zero diagonal
models.local_r2: Same Hebbian weights restricted to the 5x5 neighbourhood (open boundary), zero diagonal
models.explicit_decoder: Output the stored pattern with maximal overlap with the cue on visible cells (maximum-likelihood identification for equiprobable patterns); the antecedent 'erasure code with explicit decoder'

dynamics: Asynchronous deterministic sweeps in raster order, s_i <- sign(h_i), h_i = sum_j W_ij s_j; h_i = 0 keeps s_i, and a cell still at 0 becomes +1; at most 50 sweeps or until a sweep changes nothing
cue: Target pattern; a uniformly chosen fraction f of cells erased to 0; Gaussian noise sigma added to visible cells; initial state sign(cue) on visible cells and 0 on erased cells

replication.unit_of_analysis: memory instance (pattern set); cues inside an instance are not independent

endpoints.E1_exact_repair: fraction of cues whose final state equals the target exactly (decoder: target identified)
endpoints.E2_final_overlap: mean (1/N) sum_i s_i xi_i of the final state with the target
endpoints.E3_storage: fraction of stored patterns that are fixed points when started undamaged (Hopfield models only)
endpoints.E4_basin_identification: fraction of cues whose final state is closer (Hamming) to the target than to every other stored pattern

analysis: Descriptive per grid cell: instance-level means with t95 across the 20 instances; paired differences global minus local_r1 and global minus local_r2 by instance with t95; no multiplicity adjustment; no confirmatory claim

registered_predictions.PR1: For rand patterns, global_hopfield E1 >= local_r1 and >= local_r2 in every cell with K >= 2 (locality lowers capacity)
registered_predictions.PR2: explicit_decoder E1 >= every Hopfield model in every cell
registered_predictions.PR3: For smooth patterns no direction is registered (exploratory)

interpretation_rule: If the local fields are dominated by global Hopfield and by the explicit decoder in every cell, a memory-repair bet for local fields must justify locality by other gains (cost, locality of repair, persistence) and cannot claim superior storage at equal state size
limits: Binary Hopfield variants, not the learned NeuroPixel rule
resources: CPU numpy only, two threads; no Torch, no GPU
